facts: A new algorithm is proposed for novel view generation in one-to-one teleconferencing applications.
Two cameras are placed on either side of a computer monitor.
The proposed algorithm synthesises images from a virtual camera in arbitrary position to facilitate eye contact.
The virtual camera is typically located within the monitor.
The technique is based on an improved, dynamic-programming, stereo algorithm for efficient novel-view generation.
The paper contributes a new type of three-plane graph for dense-stereo dynamic-programming.
A new type of three-plane graph for dense-stereo dynamic-programming encourages correct occlusion labeling.
The paper contributes a compact geometric derivation for novel-view synthesis by direct projection of the minimum-cost surface.
The paper presents a novel algorithm for the temporal maintenance of a background model.
The novel algorithm for the temporal maintenance of a background model enhances the rendering of occlusions.
The novel algorithm for the temporal maintenance of a background model reduces temporal artefacts (flicker).
A cost aggregation algorithm acts directly on three-dimensional matching cost space.
Examples are given that demonstrate the robustness of the new algorithm to spatial and temporal artefacts for long stereo video streams.
Demonstrations include synthesis of cyclopean views of extended conversational sequences.
Synthesis from a freely translating virtual camera is demonstrated.
